title: The Drawer Library
bodyMd:
Three portions of this passage are marked with a bracketed number and shown in **bold**. Each question names the portion it asks about.

**Paragraph 1.** When Marisol Ferrer took over the reference desk at the Cedar Hollow Public Library, the building’s oldest card catalogue was being used to store extension cords. She emptied the drawers, labelled them by plant family, and filled them with envelopes of seed donated by gardeners around town.

**Paragraph 2.** Borrowing is simple. A patron takes up to six packets a season and, if the harvest goes well, returns a spoonful of dried seed in the autumn. There are no due dates and no fines. Ferrer keeps a ledger anyway, because it tells her which varieties thrive in the **[1] towns** short growing season and which ones gardeners quietly abandon.

**Paragraph 3.** The collection has become a record of a changing climate. Snap beans that once needed ninety frost-free days now finish a week early, and a heat-tolerant okra that nobody requested in the library’s first two summers is now the most borrowed packet on the shelf. **[2]** Every October Ferrer sends her ledger totals to a regional agricultural extension office, which has begun citing the seed library in its planting advice for the county.

**Paragraph 4.** Ferrer is **[3] modest and unassuming about** the project. It is not an experiment, she says. It is a library doing what libraries do: keeping something in circulation so that it does not disappear.
accessibilityText: A four-paragraph prose passage about a public librarian in the invented town of Cedar Hollow who turns an unused card catalogue into a seed-lending collection, and about what the borrowing records reveal about the local growing season. Three spots in the passage are marked for editing. Marked spot one, in paragraph two, is the word "towns" in the phrase "the towns short growing season". Marked spot two is a point in paragraph three, after the sentence about snap beans and okra and before the sentence beginning "Every October". Marked spot three, in paragraph four, is the phrase "modest and unassuming about" in the sentence "Ferrer is modest and unassuming about the project."

provenance.notes: Original passage. Cedar Hollow, Marisol Ferrer and every detail in the passage are invented; nothing here is drawn from or modelled on a published ACT English passage.
